triage.reviewer: independent LLM path review (glm-5.3 via Claude Code agent harness)

triage.method: Every codeFlow of every formal result was read from pass5.sarif and re-verified line-by-line against the pre-fix piccolo source tree (dataset/codeql_databases/sql_injection_dbs/piccolo_vuln, matching DB sha e4946d8). Execution chains (DDL.run -> Engine.run_ddl -> asyncpg fetch / aiosqlite execute; Query._run -> Engine.run_querystring -> compile_string -> fetch) were traced to the real driver call sites. No PyVul ground-truth files, CVE pages, or fix commits were read; the only advisory used is the one supplied in the review request itself (for the vulnerability-hit analysis section).

summary.note_on_duplicates: Results 9/10, 11/12, 13/14, 15/16 are pairwise duplicates at the same sink line: one alert from the engineSqlTextSink model (connection.execute argument 0) and one from the savepointStatementFstringSink model (the f-string itself). They describe the same underlying flow; 4 unique vulnerable statements are covered.

path: engine.run_ddl -> postgres.py:553 connection.fetch(ddl) / sqlite run_ddl -> connection.execute - real driver execution
alerts.controllable_sql_part: Everything after 'RENAME TO ' - the new table name is interpolated completely unquoted, so arbitrary SQL can be appended to the ALTER statement.
alerts.barrier_evidence: None. No quoting, escaping, or identifier allowlist anywhere on this channel; the QueryString bound-parameter channel does not apply to DDL identifier positions.
alerts.preconditions: An embedding application passes an attacker-influenced string as new_name to Alter.rename_table. No in-snapshot flow exists: the only library caller (migration_manager.py:690) passes a reflected DB table name (second-order, developer-controlled).
alerts.reasoning: The path is real and the code matches the SARIF flow exactly: API param -> dataclass field (ctorArgToFieldRead) -> unquoted f-string -> DDL executed verbatim by the engine driver. This is structurally the same defect class as the confirmed savepoint vulnerability (name-type parameter interpolated unescaped into executed SQL). However, schema/DDL APIs are migration/admin-facing, no untrusted data reaches them inside this project, and they are not covered by any known piccolo security fix. Plausible latent CWE-89, but exploitability is application-dependent.

criteria_findings.parameterization_barrier: no - not applicable to identifier positions

alerts.controllable_sql_part: Both the column name and new_name are wrapped in double quotes but with no escaping of '"' - a double quote in either value breaks out of the identifier and injects SQL structure. The two codeFlows (column and new_name) are both valid.
alerts.barrier_evidence: None. Double quotes are cosmetic, not a barrier (no doubling/escaping of embedded quotes).
alerts.preconditions: Embedding app passes attacker-influenced strings to rename_column. No in-snapshot untrusted caller.
alerts.reasoning: Same class as result 0: quoted-but-unescaped identifier interpolation into really-executed DDL. Real path, verified execution chain, but schema-API context and no in-project attacker flow make the practical risk application-dependent.

path: ' USING ' + expression interpolated verbatim, completely unquoted
DDL.run -> engine.run_ddl -> connection.fetch/execute - real driver execution
alerts.controllable_sql_part: Everything after 'USING ' - the expression is appended verbatim with no quoting at all, so this is a full raw-SQL-fragment channel.
alerts.barrier_evidence: None. The using_expression parameter is documented (docstring alter.py:396-406) as a raw SQL expression hint ('my_column_name::integer'), i.e. by contract the caller supplies SQL.
alerts.preconditions: Embedding app passes attacker-influenced string as using_expression. No in-snapshot caller passes anything but literals.
alerts.reasoning: Borderline. The path and execution are real, but the parameter is by documented contract a SQL expression fragment - closer in character to the by-design raw-SQL APIs (Table.raw/WhereRaw) than to a name-type parameter. Flagging the API's own SQL-fragment parameter is tautological (source = the same parameter whose value becomes the sink). Kept as uncertain rather than likely_fp because the docstring does not explicitly say 'arbitrary SQL executes here', and verbatim unquoted interpolation of a 'hint' parameter is easy for an app developer to misuse.

DDL.run -> engine.run_ddl -> connection.fetch/execute - real driver execution

alerts.preconditions: Embedding app passes attacker-influenced constraint_name. In-snapshot, drop_constraint is called from drop_foreign_key_constraint (alter.py:503) with a name derived from table/column metadata, not external input.
alerts.reasoning: Same defect class as results 0/1 but with a completely unquoted identifier - structurally identical to the savepoint vulnerability pattern (name-type param, unquoted, executed). Still application-dependent for exploitation and not part of the known fix.

path: (downstream, outside the reported path) where-clause assembly -> Query._run -> engine.run_querystring -> compile_string -> connection.fetch
alerts.controllable_sql_part: The entire SQL template of the where clause - by the documented design of the API.
alerts.barrier_evidence: The API offers a bound-parameter channel (docstring: WhereRaw("name = {}", value)); only the template argument is the sink, and values in the bound channel are correctly NOT reported. But the template itself is by contract raw SQL.
alerts.preconditions: An embedding app would have to pass attacker-influenced text as the SQL template - i.e. deliberately use a documented dangerous raw-SQL API with tainted SQL. Nothing like that exists anywhere in this snapshot.
alerts.reasoning: The source is the raw API's own template parameter and the sink is the QueryString construction one local step later, so the alert is tautological - it fires on the API definition itself, not on any flow of untrusted data (codeFlow has exactly 2 adjacent nodes). The template is genuinely executed verbatim downstream (verified: Query.run -> run_querystring -> compile_string keeps template text, only '{}' becomes $n/? placeholders), so the channel is real, but WhereRaw is an explicitly documented 'Execute raw SQL queries ... use with caution!' API whose purpose is to run caller-supplied SQL. Within this snapshot all call sites (docstring examples, library internals) pass literal templates with bound values. Per review criteria 6 (mis-flagging a project's by-design raw-SQL API as injection) this is a false positive for this project, with the caveat that app misuse with tainted templates would be injectable.

criteria_findings.sink_really_executes_sql: sink node is object construction; execution is real but one default-hop downstream of the reported path
criteria_findings.parameterization_barrier: values are parameterizable; the template is raw SQL by design

vulnerability_hit_analysis.task: Was the project's real CWE-89 vulnerability (piccolo commit 82679eb8, GHSA-xq59-7jf3-rjc6 - savepoint name SQL injection) hit by the formal Pass 5 results?
vulnerability_hit_analysis.source_tree_state: The analyzed source tree is the pre-fix version: postgres.py:127-139 / sqlite.py:306-319 / postgres.py:237-240 / sqlite.py:414-417 match the advisory code_before verbatim; no validate_savepoint_name exists anywhere in the tree.

advisory_functions.hit_details: No formal result at postgres.py:239. The source model (ddlIdentifierBoundary) covers Savepoint.__init__(name) and Transaction.rollback_to(savepoint_name) but NOT the name parameter of Transaction.savepoint itself, so the direct SAVEPOINT-statement injection is missed. Indirect partial coverage: the name passed to savepoint() is stored in the returned Savepoint object (postgres.py:240), and its later execution in rollback_to()/release() IS reported by results 9-12.

Results 9 and 10 (duplicate pair at postgres.py:133, both sink models), with valid codeFlows from Savepoint.__init__(name) (postgres.py:127) and from PostgresTransaction.rollback_to(savepoint_name) (postgres.py:225 -> 229), matching the advisory chain exactly.
Results 11 and 12 (duplicate pair at postgres.py:138), same source flows as rollback_to.
Same gap as postgres: Transaction.savepoint's name parameter is not a modeled source. Partially covered indirectly via the returned Savepoint's rollback_to/release (results 13-16).
Results 13 and 14 (duplicate pair at sqlite.py:313), flows from Savepoint.__init__(name) (sqlite.py:307) and SQLiteTransaction.rollback_to(savepoint_name) (sqlite.py:402 -> 406).
Results 15 and 16 (duplicate pair at sqlite.py:318), same source flows.

vulnerability_hit_analysis.verdict: HIT (substantially). The real CWE-89 vulnerability - user-provided savepoint names interpolated unquoted into f-strings and executed via connection.execute - is reported by 8 formal Pass 5 alerts (4 unique vulnerable statements: ROLLBACK TO SAVEPOINT and RELEASE SAVEPOINT in both the postgres and sqlite engines). 4 of the 6 advisory functions (rollback_to and release in both engines) are directly hit at the exact vulnerable lines with valid source-to-execution paths. The savepoint() function's own direct injection point (SAVEPOINT {name} at postgres.py:239 / sqlite.py:416) is missed because the source model omits Transaction.savepoint's name parameter, though the same tainted value is caught when it later reaches the flagged rollback_to/release sinks. Root cause of the partial miss: p5-src-008 models Savepoint.__init__(name) and rollback_to(savepoint_name) but not savepoint(name).
vulnerability_hit_analysis.hit_function_count: 4 of 6 advisory functions directly hit; 8 of 18 formal alerts are the vulnerability (results 9-16)

cross_cutting_observations: No SARIF parsing diagnostics, no native CodeQL py/sql-injection baseline results, and no other-category (NoSQL etc.) findings are mixed into the formal results: the run contains a single rule (py/augur/piccolo/pass5-sql-injection) with 18 results, executionSuccessful=true, and 353 level=none telemetry notifications only.

The reported sinks all correspond to genuinely executed SQL or (for results 5/17) to template constructions whose compiled output is executed verbatim one default-step downstream - verified against query/base.py:179-193, postgres.py:525-560, sqlite.py:590-630, querystring.py:163-192.

The bound-parameter channel is correctly excluded: QueryString.compile_string emits $n/? placeholders and keeps args separate, and only argument 0 of fetch/execute/cursor is a sink, so no parameterized value is reported (no false positives of that class among the 18).

Minor model artifact (does not change any verdict): the ctorArgToFieldRead/initParamToFieldRead summaries wire construction sites of the identically-named Savepoint class across engine files (sqlite.py:406 -> postgres.py:133 and postgres.py:229 -> sqlite.py:313), producing cross-engine flow renderings; each engine's real sink is independently and correctly reported.

All 8 savepoint alerts and the 7 'uncertain' channel alerts use API-parameter sources with no in-snapshot untrusted caller; this is the declared ORM-library trust model (embedding application boundary). Only the savepoint channels are confirmed by the project's own security fix.
